WHERE id = ?',            (title, body, payload, note_id),        )        connection.commit()        updated_row = connection.execute(            'SELECT id, title, body, tags FROM notes WHERE id = ?',            (note_id,),        ).fetchone()        return _to_note(updated_row)    finally:        _release(connection)
output.hypothesis: The current update_note implementation performs two full table scans (SELECT * FROM notes) to check existence and retrieve the updated record, plus a VACUUM-like inefficiency in logic. By replacing the full table scan with a targeted SELECT ... WHERE id = ?, we reduce the operation from O(N) to O(log N) or O(1) depending on index usage, significantly lowering CPU time and I/O for updates. This addresses the high cumulative time in update_note (1.722s) and the excessive function calls in _to_note caused by processing all rows.
risks: None. The logic remains functionally identical: check existence, update, return updated note.
The connection handling is preserved with try/finally to ensure _release is called even if an exception occurs.
No API contract changes; response format and error handling (404 via None return) are preserved.
